label: Adenoid_Cystic_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Malignant salivary tumor with characteristic biphasic ductal and myoepithelial cell composition
- Most common in minor salivary glands (palate); can occur in parotid and submandibular glands
- Grows in cribriform, tubular, and solid patterns (solid pattern = adverse prognosis)
- Perineural invasion is frequent and classic
- 60–90% have MYB–NFIB or MYBL1–NFIB fusions ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- High risk of late local recurrence and metastasis, especially to lung

## Terminology

- Adenoid cystic carcinoma (AdCC); “cylindroma” is obsolete
- Abbreviations: AdCC, ACC

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Infiltrative malignant neoplasm with dual cell population (ductal/luminal and myoepithelial/basal) ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=265), [Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - Growth in cribriform, tubular, and/or solid architectural patterns
  - Basophilic or eosinophilic “pseudocystic” spaces containing basement-membrane-like matrix (PAS+, Alcian blue+)
  - Frequent perineural invasion
  - Diagnosis is based on tissue findings of typical histology or molecular evidence of fusion involving MYB, MYBL1, or NFIB genes ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- **Desirable:**
  - Positive MYB immunostaining (nuclear), especially in cytology ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1066))
  - Ki-67 labeling index higher in solid areas
  - Immunophenotype supporting both ductal and myoepithelial differentiation

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- 60–90% harbor MYB–NFIB or MYBL1–NFIB fusion ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- May arise in any major/minor salivary gland or outside glands (e.g., trachea, skin, breast, etc.)
- Tumorigenesis involves MYB-driven transcriptional deregulation

## Clinical Issues

- **Epidemiology:** ~10% of malignant salivary gland tumors ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=265)); M=F; mean age ~57 ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- **Site:** Most common in minor glands (palate), then parotid, submandibular, and others ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304), [Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1062)), [Fig. 20-72](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p1062_fig01_fig_20_72.jpeg)
- **Presentation:** Palatal mass/ulcer; slow-growing, firm, potentially painful due to perineural spread; often adults, 5th–7th decades
- **Natural history:** Local recurrence and late hematogenous lung metastasis frequent; regional nodal spread less common ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1327))
- **Treatment:** Complete excision + adjuvant radiotherapy often used due to recurrence risk

## Staging

- No WHO-endorsed grading system ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- **Proposed grades:**
  - Grade 1: no solid component
  - Grade 2 (intermediate grade): 1–29% solid component ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - Grade 3 (high grade): ≥30% solid component (solid pattern = high grade) ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))

## Macroscopic

- Firm, poorly circumscribed, gray-white mass; size variable
- Minor gland tumors may ulcerate mucosa ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=305))
- ![Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the palate](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_oral/hn_oral_p0305_fig01_figure_8_49.jpeg)
- ![Cut section, adenoid cystic carcinoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticgross01.jpg)

## Microscopic

- Cribriform (“Swiss cheese”), tubular, and solid patterns ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - **Cribriform:** Basaloid nests with true/pseudo-lumina and basophilic or eosinophilic matrix (PAS+, Alcian blue+)
    - ![Cribriform pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu03new.jpg)
  - **Tubular:** Small duct-like spaces with biphasic cell population
    - ![Tubular pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu02new.jpg)
  - **Solid:** Sheets/nests of basaloid cells, frequent mitoses, necrosis; adverse prognosis
    - ![Solid pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu04new.jpg)
- Frequent, sometimes extensive perineural invasion ([Hn Biopsy Interpretation](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Biopsy_Interpretation.pdf#page=122)), ![Perineural invasion](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu06new.jpg)
- Dual population: ductal (cuboidal, eosinophilic) and abluminal myoepithelial (basaloid) ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=265))
- Pseudocystic spaces with glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix (PAS+, Alcian blue+) ([Hn Thompson](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Thompson.pdf#page=341))
  - ![Pseudocysts with matrix](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_thompson/hn_thompson_p0341_fig01_figure_13_31.jpg)
- Solid/high-grade areas may show necrosis
- Occasional clear cell, squamous, or high-grade transformation ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=306))
- Mitoses generally low, but higher in solid/high-grade foci
- ![Cribriform and tubular patterns](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_thompson/hn_thompson_p0337_fig01_figure_13_26.jpg)

## Cytology

- Clusters/balls/cords of basaloid cells, sometimes with matrix “globules” ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- May be paucicellular or hypercellular, hyaline/myxoid background
- ![Diff-Quik smear](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu14new.jpg)
- ![Papanicolaou smear](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu16new.jpg)
- Milan system: “Malignant”

## Ancillary Tests

- **IHC:**
  - MYB: nuclear+, ~80% (diagnostic aid) ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1066)), ![MYB nuclear staining](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu13new.jpg)
  - p63/p40: basal/myoepithelial cells ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1066)), ![p40](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu10new.jpg)
  - SMA, calponin, S100, SOX10: support myoepithelial differentiation ([Hn Thompson](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Thompson.pdf#page=339)), ![SMA](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu11new.jpg)
  - CD117: luminal cells ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1066))
- **Molecular:** MYB–NFIB or MYBL1–NFIB fusion in most ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html)); confirm by FISH/RT-PCR if diagnosis uncertain

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Polymorphous adenocarcinoma:**
  - More cytologic monotony, less perineural invasion, lacks biphasic pattern and pronounced cribriforming; MYB negative ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304))
- **Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma:**
  - Biphasic but clear cells, lacks cribriform “blue goo,” often lower grade; immunophenotype overlaps ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Epithelial_Myoepithelial_Carcinoma.html))
- **Basal cell adenoma/adenocarcinoma:**
  - May mimic solid/cribriform but lacks matrix pseudocysts and perineural invasion; more prominent palisading ([Hn Thompson](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Thompson.pdf#page=339))
- **Pleomorphic adenoma:**
  - Matrix globules/chondromyxoid stroma, no invasive/perineural growth, cytologically bland
- **Myoepithelial carcinoma:**
  - Overlap but lacks true ductal/cribriform features
- **Clear cell carcinoma:**
  - No characteristic matrix or biphasic pattern; defined by EWSR1 fusions ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsclearcellcarcinoma.html))
- **HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma:**
  - Sinonasal location, HPV+, lacks MYB fusion ([Hn Gnepp](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Gnepp.pdf#page=157))
- **Adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma:**
  - Primitive histology, young age, EWSR1 rearrangement ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Sialoblastoma.html))
- **Salivary duct carcinoma:**
  - High-grade, apocrine features, comedonecrosis; androgen receptor+/HER2+ on IHC ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssalivaryductcarcinoma.html))
- **Squamous cell carcinoma:**
  - Prominent keratinization, squamous markers, lacks biphasic architecture
- **Microsecretory adenocarcinoma:**
  - Shows microcystic pattern, S100+, low grade
- **Hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma:**
  - Low-grade, cords of clear cells with hyalinized stroma; EWSR1 fusions ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/lunghyalinizingclearcellcarcinoma.html))
- **Sclerosing microcystic adenocarcinoma:**
  - Sclerotic stroma, microcystic pattern
- **Sebaceous adenocarcinoma:**
  - Sebaceous components, cytoplasmic vacuolation; immunoprofile distinct ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssebaceousadenoma.html))

## Prognostic Factors

- Presence/percentage of solid architecture is strongest predictor (≥30% = higher risk; any solid is adverse)
- High mitotic rate (≥5/10 hpf), high-grade transformation, positive/close margins, lymphovascular and perineural/intraneural invasion increase risk ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- Age, sinonasal location, and female sex linked to worse outcome in some studies
- Ki-67 high in solid/poorly differentiated areas ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1068))
- 5-year survival 55–89%; 15–20 year survival 10–40% ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))

## Illustrative Cases

- 27F, parotid AdCC with high-grade transformation
- 70F, soft palate AdCC with perineural extension to orbits
- 36M, tracheal AdCC (autopsy)
- 70M, laryngeal AdCC

cards.excerpt: Entity: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma definition: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma (HMSC) is an epithelial neoplasm exhibiting features of both surface-derived and minor salivary gland–derived elements, harbouring transcriptionally active HPV. related_terminology: Acceptable: HPV-associated multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma. Not recommended: HPV-related carcinoma with adenoid cystic–like features. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a carcinoma composed of basaloid type cells; high-risk HPV by HPV-specific assay (not p16 alone); myoepithelial differentiation by immunohistochemistry. Desirable: sinonasal tract location; ductal differentiation; overlying squamous dysplasia.

cards.title: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma Section: cytology FNAB smears can show poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma or salivary duct carcinoma, or other salivary gland carcinomas including mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma, or the FNAB may show PA, depending on sampling. It is uncommon that both components are identified, and necrosis in an otherwise pleomorphic adenoma may be the only clue apart from a previous history of a longstanding mass or previous biopsy.

cards.title: Sialoblastoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Sialoblastoma definition: Sialoblastoma is a low-grade malignant primitive salivary gland anlage neoplasm. related_terminology: Not recommended: embryoma; basaloid adenocarcinoma; congenital basal cell adenoma; congenital hybrid basal cell adenoma; adenoid cystic carcinoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a salivary gland malignancy showing primitive solid organoid nests; basaloid epithelial cells with vesicular chromatin; cuboidal to columnar ductal cells. Desirable: dividing fibrous stroma and peripheral palisading.

cards.title: Sialoblastoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Sialoblastoma Section: differential_diagnosis The primitive histological features and the patients young age help to differentiate sialoblastoma from other basaloid salivary gland tumours such as basal cell adenoma/adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma.

cards.title: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes other salivary gland tumours with biphasic and/or clear cell morphology, such as adenoid cystic carcinoma, basal cell adenocarcinoma, pleomorphic adenoma, myoepithelial carcinoma, and clear cell carcinoma.

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:
Characterized by a propensity of perineural invasion, high frequency of local and distant recurrence and poor long term prognosis (Eur J Cancer 2015;51:2768, Head Neck 2017;39:456, Braz J Otorhinolaryngol 2015;81:329, Head Neck 2014;36:998)
5 year overall survival 55 - 89%
15 year or 20 year survival is dismal, in the range of 20 - 40%
Rates of local recurrence and distant metastasis are 16 - 67% and 8 - 46%
Lung is most common site of distant metastasis (Head Neck 2017;39:456)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Lung metastases
cards.excerpt:
Prognostic factors
Independent prognostic predictors include AJCC TNM staging, margin status, high mitotic index (defined as ≥ 5 per 10 high power fields) and solid architecture (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422)
Presence and percentage of solid architecture reflects clinical outcome and should be reported in the pathology report
Some studies showed that the presence but not the percentage of solid growth is an independent predictor for adverse outcome (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Ora Radio 2013;115:368, Head Neck 2017;39:456)
Other studies show that tumors with higher percentage of solid pattern, defined as 30% or more, are associated with increased risk of recurrence and decreased survival (Cancer 1984;54:1062, Cancer 1978;42:265)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Complete surgical resection with appropriate margins is the mainstream treatment
Most patients receive adjuvant radiation therapy given the high rate of local recurrence and dismal long term survival

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Essential features
cards.heading: Essential features
cards.text_excerpt:
Arises from submucosal minor salivary glands of the larynx (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279)
Most common salivary gland malignancy of the larynx (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
3 histological growth patterns including tubular, cribriform and solid (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
Slow growing infiltrative tumor often presenting at an advanced stage with a predilection for perineural involvement and propensity for local recurrence and metastasis (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Epidemiology
cards.heading: Epidemiology
cards.text_excerpt:
Likely near equal M:F ratio
Slight female predominance (~57% female) was found in a SEER database review, though a literature review by Marchiano et al. found a slight male predominance (Ear Nose Throat J 2022;101:587, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
Onset occurs at any age during adulthood (20 - 90 years) but more commonly between fifth and sixth decade (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433, Ear Nose Throat J 2022;101:587)
Rare case reports in those < 18 years old (Kulak Burun Bogaz Ihtis Derg 2008;18:319, Ear Nose Throat J 2002;81:34)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Pathophysiology
cards.heading: Pathophysiology
cards.text_excerpt:
Associated with translocation t(6;9)(q22-23;p23-24), which results in fusion of the MYB proto-oncogene and transcription factor gene nuclear factor I B (NFIB) (Mod Pathol 2011;24:1169)
Fusion between MYBL1 and NFIB genes (through a t(8;9) translocation) have been identified in MYB fusion negative tumors, indicating that genetic alterations in other members of the same transcription factor family may also be drivers for tumor development (Oncotarget 2016;7:66239, Mod Pathol 2019;32:1416)
Some laryngeal adenoid cystic carcinomas are negative for MYB::NFIB (3 out of 5 in Brill et al.) (Mod Pathol 2011;24:1169)
These may show increased copy number variation or promoter hijacking of MYB proto-oncogene (Pathology 2023;55:456)
Adenoid cystic carcinomas, including fusion negative tumors, show increased MYB mRNA (Mod Pathol 2011;24:1169)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.heading: Clinical features
cards.text_excerpt:
No predisposing risk factors known (e.g., smoking) (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279, Medicine (Baltimore) 2019;98:e18177)
Most commonly presents as a submucosal mass or masses (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279)
Demonstrates a slow infiltrative growth pattern (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2022;15:79)
Most patients present with locally advanced disease (Ear Nose Throat J 2022;101:587)
Signs and symptoms relate to the anatomical location of the tumor, with dyspnea and hoarseness being the most common features (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2022;15:79)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Supraglottic: dysphagia
cards.heading: Supraglottic: dysphagia
cards.text_excerpt:
Glottic: hoarseness, pharyngeal paresthesia
Subglottic: stridor, dyspnea, airway obstruction (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279, Medicine (Baltimore) 2019;98:e18177, Oncol Lett 2018;16:2783)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Diagnosis
cards.heading: Diagnosis
cards.text_excerpt:
Diagnosis is achieved by histological examination of tissue
Evidence of MYB or MYBL1 translocation can support the diagnosis (Mod Pathol 2019;32:1416)
MYB RNA in situ hybridization may have higher sensitivity than other techniques, including fluorescent in situ hybridization (Pathology 2023;55:456)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Radiology description
cards.heading: Radiology description
cards.text_excerpt:
Computerized tomography (CT) is the most commonly used imaging modality, although Xray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and FDG PET have also been used (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
Findings on CT are often that of a poorly defined, heterogeneous mass (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
CT generally underestimates the tumor extent as adenoid cystic carcinoma can grow submucosally without producing a distinct mass (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Treatment
cards.heading: Treatment
cards.text_excerpt:
Surgical excision with wide margins has been the mainstay of treatment (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279)
Commonly total laryngectomy; however, partial laryngectomy is sometimes considered if the tumor is small and well defined with the possibility of negative surgical margins or is located in the supraglottic region (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433, Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2022;15:79)
Though adenoid cystic carcinoma is considered to be a radioresistant tumor, postoperative radiotherapy is utilized in many cases (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
Neck dissection is undertaken in those with clinical or histological nodal metastases (Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital 2009;29:279)
Adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy is less commonly employed but has been used in cases of high grade tumors or advanced spread (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2022;15:79)
Requires long term follow up due to the risk of late recurrence and distant metastasis (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2022;15:79)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Biphasic tumor composed of ductal epithelial and myoepithelial cells
cards.heading: Biphasic tumor composed of ductal epithelial and myoepithelial cells
cards.text_excerpt:
Ductal cells have eosinophilic cytoplasm with round nuclei, while myoepithelial cells have scant amounts of clear cytoplasm and angular hyperchromatic nuclei imparting a basaloid appearance
3 histological growth patterns: cribriform, tubular and solid; lesions commonly demonstrate a combination of patterns (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433, Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Cribriform is the most common pattern (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433, Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Cribriform pattern: islands of cells surrounding variably sized rigid cyst-like spaces; spaces are not true gland lumina and are continuous with surrounding stroma (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Spaces contain basophilic glycosaminoglycans or eosinophilic PAS positive basal lamina material (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Tubular pattern: separated tubules with intervening eosinophilic to hyalinized stroma; well formed ducts displaying inner epithelial and outer myoepithelial layers are more prominent (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Solid pattern: sheets of basaloid cells without tubular or pseudocystic formations; may show a greater degree of atypia, mitoses and necrosis (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — High grade transformation may rarely be seen
cards.heading: High grade transformation may rarely be seen
cards.text_excerpt:
Regions of conventional adenoid cystic carcinoma are seen alongside an area of high grade undifferentiated carcinoma or poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma
High grade regions lack ductal or myoepithelial differentiation, show increased mitoses (> 5/high power field [HPF]), comedonecrosis, focal areas of micropapillary or squamoid growth and stromal desmoplasia (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2011;135:511)
Strong tendency for perineural invasion (Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;154:433)
